title: Animals And Birds Arabic Summary For The 7th Degree Of The 1st Station

questions.question: What do the three truths lead all animal species to declare together?
questions.answer: They point all animals together to bear witness that Allah alone is truly God.

questions.question: How is the earth described when presenting this shared testimony?
questions.answer: It is pictured like one huge human being declaring Allah’s oneness in a way suitable to its greatness.

questions.question: To whom is this testimony said to be conveyed?
questions.answer: It is presented to the inhabitants of the heavens.

questions.question: What happened in the traveler’s understanding when he witnessed this scene?
questions.answer: He grasped the meaning fully and clearly.

questions.question: Which two broad groups are especially mentioned as being united in this testimony?
questions.answer: Animals and birds.

questions.question: In what two ways are animals and birds described as responding to Allah?
questions.answer: They are described as praising Him and bearing witness to Him.

questions.question: What parts of animals are treated as meaningful signs or expressions?
questions.answer: Their senses, inner capacities, limbs, organs, and bodily tools are all treated as signs.

questions.question: What qualities are given to the “words” of their senses and powers?
questions.answer: They are balanced, orderly, and expressive.

questions.question: What qualities are given to the “words” of their limbs and organs?
questions.answer: They are complete and persuasive.

questions.question: Which divine actions in the passage are connected to will?
questions.answer: Bringing beings into existence, making them, and creating them are linked to will.

questions.question: Which divine actions are connected to purpose?
questions.answer: Giving distinction and decoration is linked to purpose.

questions.question: Which divine actions are connected to wisdom?
questions.answer: Giving proper measure and forming each creature is linked to wisdom.

questions.question: From what simple beginnings do the many animal forms come forth?
questions.answer: They come from eggs and drops of sperm that are alike or very similar.

questions.question: What contrast is emphasized between the origins of animals and their final forms?
questions.answer: Their starting materials are limited and similar, but the forms that emerge are endlessly varied and distinct.

questions.question: How does this contrast strengthen the argument of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that such rich variety and order cannot come from the simple origins by themselves, but point to a deliberate Creator.

questions.question: What is the main claim made by the combined witness of animals in the passage?
questions.answer: Their united condition and makeup testify to Allah’s necessary existence and His oneness.

questions.question: Why does the passage speak of a “consensus” among animals and birds?
questions.answer: Because all their kinds, taken together, point in the same direction and give one shared testimony.

questions.question: What image is used to help the reader imagine the earth’s testimony?
questions.answer: The earth is imagined as if it were one giant person speaking with a single voice.

questions.question: What did the traveler do after seeing this sign?
questions.answer: He understood its meaning completely.

questions.question: How are the senses and powers of animals presented in the passage?
questions.answer: They are presented like meaningful speech that reflects order and eloquence.

questions.question: How are their body parts and organs presented?
questions.answer: They are shown as powerful signs that communicate completeness and purpose.

questions.question: Name the three major categories of divine activity mentioned in the passage.
questions.answer: Creating, distinguishing and beautifying, and measuring and shaping.

questions.question: What does the link between creation and will teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that living beings are brought into existence intentionally, not randomly.

questions.question: What does the link between measuring and shaping teach?
questions.answer: It teaches that their forms are arranged with wisdom and precise order.

questions.question: Why are eggs and sperm mentioned?
questions.answer: They are mentioned to show that many different creatures come from origins that are very similar and limited.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from the emergence of endless forms out of similar beginnings?
questions.answer: Such emergence is taken as a definite sign of divine power, knowledge, and wisdom.

questions.question: According to the passage, what united message is being testified to by all species of animals?
questions.answer: That there is no true deity except Allah.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the agreement of the three truths mean in simple terms?
questions.answer: It means those three lines of evidence support one another and arrive at the same conclusion.

questions.question: What larger reality is symbolized by the earth speaking like a great man?
questions.answer: It symbolizes the whole created world giving one coordinated witness to Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What role does the traveler play in this part of the passage?
questions.answer: He serves as the observer who recognizes and understands the testimony found in creation.

questions.question: Which living creatures are directly named in the formal statement that follows?
questions.answer: All animals and birds are directly named.

questions.question: Besides existing, what two devotional functions do these creatures perform?
questions.answer: They praise Allah and testify to Him.

questions.question: Why might the passage mention both inner faculties and outward limbs?
questions.answer: To show that both the inward and outward aspects of living beings point to their Creator.

questions.question: What is implied by saying these features are balanced and ordered?
questions.answer: It implies careful arrangement rather than accident or chaos.

questions.question: What is implied by saying they are eloquent and persuasive?
questions.answer: It implies that their very design strongly communicates meaning to anyone who reflects.

questions.question: How are purpose and wisdom treated in relation to animal forms?
questions.answer: They are presented as guiding principles behind the differences, beauty, proportions, and shapes of creatures.

questions.question: What does “definite indication” suggest about the strength of the argument?
questions.answer: It suggests that the evidence is presented as clear, firm, and not doubtful.

questions.question: What two characteristics are given for the origins of these creatures?
questions.answer: Their origins are described as similar to one another and limited in number.

questions.question: What two characteristics are given for the resulting forms of these creatures?
questions.answer: Their forms are described as ordered and endlessly varied.

questions.question: What final conclusion is reached from the three truths mentioned at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: Together they establish a shared witness from all animal species to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Why is the testimony of animals presented as collective rather than individual?
questions.answer: Because the argument depends on the agreement of all kinds of animals, which makes the witness broader and stronger.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the earth and a human being?
questions.answer: The earth is compared to an enormous person speaking one declaration of faith.

questions.question: What does this comparison help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader imagine the world as a unified sign instead of disconnected creatures.

questions.question: What was the traveler’s response to this vision of the earth?
questions.answer: He fully understood the meaning contained in it.

questions.question: In the Arabic-based declaration explained in English, what do animals and birds do besides merely living?
questions.answer: They actively praise Allah and testify to Him through their whole makeup.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by the “words” of their senses and powers?
questions.answer: It means the way those faculties are arranged speaks symbolically of design and divine authorship.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by the “words” of their limbs and instruments?
questions.answer: It means their bodily structures communicate purpose, function, and completeness.

questions.question: How does the passage connect creation with will, distinction with purpose, and shaping with wisdom?
questions.answer: It presents each as a deliberate divine act with a fitting attribute behind it.

questions.question: Why is it important that these forms are described as orderly?
questions.answer: Order shows regulation and intention rather than confusion.

questions.question: Why is it important that these forms are described as distinct and varied?
questions.answer: Variety shows creative richness and specific determination for each creature.

questions.question: What is the significance of saying the forms are beyond counting while their material origins are limited?
questions.answer: It highlights an extraordinary transformation that points beyond material causes to divine action.

questions.question: What beginnings are named for the emergence of animal life?
questions.answer: Eggs and sperm drops are named as the beginnings.

questions.question: Summarize the passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: The passage teaches that the full structure, diversity, and origin of animals and birds together form a powerful witness to Allah’s necessary existence and unity.

questions.question: What shared act of witness do all animal species perform according to the passage?
questions.answer: They all join in testifying to Allah’s sole divinity.

questions.question: What does the phrase “by the consensus” add to the meaning of this witness?
questions.answer: It shows that multiple signs and all kinds of creatures support the same truth together.

questions.question: What does the passage say the traveler gained from seeing this?
questions.answer: He reached a complete understanding of what this testimony meant.

questions.question: Which creatures are specifically included in the formal declaration?
questions.answer: Every kind of animal and bird.

questions.question: Through what inward features do they bear witness?
questions.answer: Through their senses, capacities, and subtle faculties.

questions.question: Through what outward features do they bear witness?
questions.answer: Through their limbs, organs, members, and bodily means.

questions.question: Why might both inward and outward features matter in the argument?
questions.answer: Because the whole creature, inside and out, is presented as evidence of divine design.

questions.question: What characteristics of these features make them convincing signs?
questions.answer: They are proportioned, organized, complete, and expressive.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about how animals are brought into existence?
questions.answer: They are brought into existence through divine willing, not through mindless processes alone.

questions.question: What does it teach about the differences and beauty found among them?
questions.answer: These are presented as intentional and meaningful, not accidental extras.

questions.question: What does it teach about their proportions and shapes?
questions.answer: Their forms are measured and fashioned with wisdom.

questions.question: What beginnings are said to be alike or nearly alike?
questions.answer: Eggs and sperm drops.

questions.question: What result comes from those similar beginnings?
questions.answer: Innumerable, different, well-ordered forms appear.

questions.question: What central truth is all the evidence in this passage meant to support?
questions.answer: That Allah necessarily exists and is one.

questions.question: What is the function of the three truths mentioned at the opening of the passage?
questions.answer: They work together as supporting proofs that lead to one united conclusion.

questions.question: How is the earth imagined in relation to the testimony of animals?
questions.answer: It is imagined as one vast speaker declaring Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does this image imply about the relationship between individual creatures and the planet as a whole?
questions.answer: It implies that all creatures together form one coordinated testimony across the earth.

questions.question: What was the traveler able to do after observing this sign?
questions.answer: He was able to understand its message completely.

questions.question: How are animals and birds described in religious terms?
questions.answer: They are described as beings that praise Allah and testify to Him.

questions.question: What is the meaning of describing their faculties as “words”?
questions.answer: Their faculties function like signs that communicate truth without ordinary speech.

questions.question: What is added by saying their bodily parts are also like “words”?
questions.answer: It shows that their physical design, not just their inner capacities, points to Allah.

questions.question: Which divine quality is stressed in connection with bringing creatures into existence?
questions.answer: Divine will.

questions.question: Which divine quality is stressed in connection with making creatures different and beautiful?
questions.answer: Purpose.

questions.question: Which divine quality is stressed in connection with giving them measured forms?
questions.answer: Wisdom.

questions.question: Why does the passage keep emphasizing order and proportion?
questions.answer: Because these qualities support the idea of intentional design and wise arrangement.

questions.question: Why are limited and similar origins important in the argument?
questions.answer: They make the emergence of endless, distinct forms even more striking as a sign of divine power.

questions.question: What kind of diversity is described in the resulting creatures?
questions.answer: Their forms are organized, different from one another, varied, and beyond counting.

questions.question: If you had to state the passage’s reasoning as cause and effect, how would you put it?
questions.answer: Since similar and limited biological beginnings produce countless ordered and purposeful creatures, this points to a willing, wise, and purposeful Creator.
